newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog seeks tougher rules on water firms.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog seeks tougher rules on water firms.

text.p: Britain's water industry regulator Ofwat on Wednesday published proposals to toughen rules governing water firms' unregulated business interests.
Water firms are required to keep unregulated or non-core activities at "arms length" from their main water supply and sewerage businesses to prevent cross-subsidy.

The existing rules were designed to ensure that companies could not pass on costs from any non-core activities to consumers. But investigations last year into the way firms traded with their associated companies showed they were not sticking to Ofwat's guidelines.

The regulator now wants the firms to put more emphasis on market testing and competitive letting of contracts and to report on any indirect transactions with associates. Ofwat also wants auditors to play a greater role in reporting on compliance with the guidelines.
The regulator is asking for comments on the proposals by February 21.

Ofwat's report on its investigation into the firms' trading practices, published last year, found that the degree of competitive tendering varied widely and decisions on contracts and post tender negotiations were not always clearly documented.

It found potential for conflict of interest where directors or senior managers of the regulated business held directorships in associated companies. And in some firms charges paid by the regulated business to the group were not directly linked to the services provided. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
